entries.originalText: In all that thou doest, remember the end, and how thou wilt stand before a strict judge, from whom nothing is hid, who is not bribed with gifts, nor accepteth excuses, but will judge righteous judgment.
entries.modernizedText: In all you do, remember the end and how you will stand before a strict judge from whom nothing is hidden, who is not bribed with gifts and accepts no excuses, but will judge with righteous judgment.

entries.originalText: O most miserable and foolish sinner, who art sometimes in fear of the countenance of an angry man, what wilt thou answer to God, who knoweth all thy misdeeds?
entries.modernizedText: Oh, most miserable and foolish sinner, who sometimes fears the face of an angry person, what will you answer to God, who knows all your misdeeds?

entries.originalText: Why dost thou not provide for thyself against the day of judgment, when no man shall be able to be excused or defended by means of another, but each one shall bear his burden himself alone?
entries.modernizedText: Why do you not prepare yourself for the day of judgment, when no one will be able to be excused or defended by another, but each will bear his burden alone?

entries.originalText: Now doth thy labour bring forth fruit, now is thy weeping acceptable, thy groaning heard, thy sorrow well pleasing to God, and cleansing to thy soul.
entries.modernizedText: Now your labor brings forth fruit, now your weeping is acceptable, your groaning heard, your sorrow pleasing to God and cleansing to your soul.

entries.originalText: Even here on earth the patient man findeth great occasion of purifying his soul.
entries.modernizedText: Even here on earth the patient person finds great opportunity to purify his soul.

entries.originalText: When suffering injuries he grieveth more for the other’s malice than for his own wrong; when he prayeth heartily for those that despitefully use him, and forgiveth them from his heart; when he is not slow to ask pardon from others; when he is swifter to pity than to anger; when he frequently denieth himself and striveth altogether to subdue the flesh to the spirit.
entries.modernizedText: When suffering injuries, he grieves more for the other’s malice than for his own wrong; he prays heartily for those who despitefully use him and forgives them from his heart; he is not slow to ask pardon from others; he is quicker to pity than to anger; he frequently denies himself and strives completely to subdue the flesh to the spirit.

entries.originalText: Better is it now to purify the soul from sin, than to cling to sins from which we must be purged hereafter.
entries.modernizedText: It is better now to purify the soul from sin than to cling to sins from which we must be purged hereafter.

entries.originalText: Truly we deceive ourselves by the inordinate love which we bear towards the flesh.
entries.modernizedText: Truly we deceive ourselves by the excessive love we bear toward the flesh.

entries.originalText: What is it which that fire shall devour, save thy sins?
entries.modernizedText: What will that fire devour except your sins?

entries.originalText: The more thou sparest thyself and followest the flesh, the more heavy shall thy punishment be, and the more fuel art thou heaping up for the burning.
entries.modernizedText: The more you spare yourself and follow the flesh, the heavier your punishment will be, and the more fuel you are heaping up for the burning.

entries.originalText: For wherein a man hath sinned, therein shall he be the more heavily punished.
entries.modernizedText: For in whatever a person has sinned, in that he will be punished more heavily.

entries.originalText: There shall the slothful be pricked forward with burning goads, and the gluttons be tormented with intolerable hunger and thirst.
entries.modernizedText: There the slothful will be driven forward with burning goads, and the gluttons tormented with intolerable hunger and thirst.

entries.originalText: There shall the luxurious and the lovers of pleasure be plunged into burning pitch and stinking brimstone, and the envious shall howl like mad dogs for very grief.
entries.modernizedText: There the luxurious and lovers of pleasure will be plunged into burning pitch and stinking brimstone, and the envious will howl like mad dogs from sheer grief.

entries.originalText: No sin will there be which shall not be visited with its own proper punishment.
entries.modernizedText: There will be no sin that is not visited with its own proper punishment.

entries.originalText: The proud shall be filled with utter confusion, and the covetous shall be pinched with miserable poverty.
entries.modernizedText: The proud will be filled with utter confusion, and the covetous will be afflicted with miserable poverty.

entries.originalText: An hour’s pain there shall be more grievous than a hundred years here of the bitterest penitence.
entries.modernizedText: An hour’s pain there will be more grievous than a hundred years of the bitterest penitence here.

entries.originalText: No quiet shall be there, no comfort for the lost, though here sometimes there is respite from pain, and enjoyment of the solace of friends.
entries.modernizedText: There will be no quiet there, no comfort for the lost, though here there is sometimes respite from pain and enjoyment of the solace of friends.

entries.originalText: Be thou anxious now and sorrowful for thy sins, that in the day of judgment thou mayest have boldness with the blessed.
entries.modernizedText: Be anxious now and sorrowful for your sins, so that on the day of judgment you may have boldness with the blessed.

entries.originalText: For then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him and made no account of his labours.(1) Then shall he stand up to judge, he who now submitteth himself in humility to the judgments of men.
entries.modernizedText: For then the righteous person will stand in great boldness before the face of those who have afflicted him and made no account of his labors.(1) Then the person who now submits himself humbly to human judgments will stand up to judge.

entries.originalText: Then shall the poor and humble man have great confidence, while the proud is taken with fear on every side.
entries.modernizedText: Then the poor and humble person will have great confidence, while the proud are taken with fear on every side.

entries.originalText: Then shall it be seen that he was the wise man in this world who learned to be a fool and despised for Christ.
entries.modernizedText: Then it will be seen that the wise person in this world was the one who learned to be a fool and despised for Christ.

entries.originalText: Then shall all tribulation patiently borne delight us, while the mouth of the ungodly shall be stopped.
entries.modernizedText: Then all tribulation patiently borne will delight us, while the mouth of the ungodly will be stopped.

entries.originalText: Then shall every godly man rejoice, and every profane man shall mourn.
entries.modernizedText: Then every godly person will rejoice, and every profane person will mourn.

entries.originalText: Then the afflicted flesh shall more rejoice than if it had been alway nourished in delights.
entries.modernizedText: Then the afflicted flesh will rejoice more than if it had always been nourished in delights.

entries.originalText: Then the humble garment shall put on beauty, and the precious robe shall hide itself as vile.
entries.modernizedText: Then the humble garment will put on beauty, and the precious robe will hide itself as vile.

entries.originalText: Then the little poor cottage shall be more commended than the gilded palace.
entries.modernizedText: Then the little poor cottage will be praised more than the gilded palace.

entries.originalText: Then enduring patience shall have more might than all the power of the world.
entries.modernizedText: Then enduring patience will have more might than all the power of the world.

entries.originalText: Then simple obedience shall be more highly exalted than all worldly wisdom.
entries.modernizedText: Then simple obedience will be exalted more highly than all worldly wisdom.

entries.originalText: Then a pure and good conscience shall more rejoice than learned philosophy.
entries.modernizedText: Then a pure and good conscience will rejoice more than learned philosophy.

entries.originalText: Then contempt of riches shall have more weight than all the treasure of the children of this world.
entries.modernizedText: Then contempt of riches will have more weight than all the treasure of the children of this world.

entries.originalText: Then shalt thou find more comfort in having prayed devoutly than in having fared sumptuously.
entries.modernizedText: Then you will find more comfort in having prayed devoutly than in having lived sumptuously.

entries.originalText: Then thou wilt rather rejoice in having kept silence than in having made long speech.
entries.modernizedText: Then you will rejoice more in having kept silence than in having made a long speech.

entries.originalText: Then holy deeds shall be far stronger than many fine words.
entries.modernizedText: Then holy deeds will be far stronger than many fine words.

entries.originalText: Then a strict life and sincere penitence shall bring deeper pleasure than all earthly delight.
entries.modernizedText: Then a strict life and sincere penitence will bring deeper pleasure than all earthly delight.

entries.originalText: Learn now to suffer a little, that then thou mayest be enabled to escape heavier sufferings.
entries.modernizedText: Learn now to suffer a little, so that then you may be enabled to escape heavier sufferings.

entries.originalText: Prove first here, what thou art able to endure hereafter.
entries.modernizedText: First test here what you are able to endure hereafter.

entries.originalText: If now thou art able to bear so little, how wilt thou be able to endure eternal torments?
entries.modernizedText: If you are now able to bear so little, how will you be able to endure eternal torments?

entries.originalText: If now a little suffering maketh thee so impatient, what shall hell-fire do then?
entries.modernizedText: If a little suffering now makes you so impatient, what will hell-fire do then?

entries.originalText: Behold of a surety thou art not able to have two Paradises, to take thy fill or delight here in this world, and to reign with Christ hereafter.
entries.modernizedText: Be assured that you cannot have two Paradises: to take your fill of delight here in this world and to reign with Christ hereafter.

entries.originalText: If even unto this day thou hadst ever lived in honours and pleasures, what would the whole profit thee if now death came to thee in an instant?
entries.modernizedText: If you had always lived in honors and pleasures even to this day, what good would the whole be to you if death now came to you in an instant?

entries.originalText: All therefore is vanity, save to love God and to serve Him only.
entries.modernizedText: All, therefore, is vanity except to love God and serve Him alone.

entries.originalText: For he who loveth God with all his heart feareth not death, nor punishment, nor judgment, nor hell, because perfect love giveth sure access to God.
entries.modernizedText: For the person who loves God with all his heart does not fear death, punishment, judgment, or hell, because perfect love gives sure access to God.

entries.originalText: But he who still delighteth in sin, no marvel if he is afraid of death and judgment.
entries.modernizedText: But if someone still delights in sin, it is no wonder that he fears death and judgment.

entries.originalText: Nevertheless it is a good thing, if love as yet cannot restrain thee from evil, that at least the fear of hell should hold thee back.
entries.modernizedText: Nevertheless, if love cannot yet restrain you from evil, it is a good thing that at least the fear of hell should hold you back.

entries.originalText: But he who putteth aside the fear of God cannot long continue in good, but shall quickly fall into the snares of the devil.
entries.modernizedText: But the person who puts aside the fear of God cannot long continue in good, but will quickly fall into the snares of the devil.
